content:
droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `process_death` (process_death): Fill the screen's form, let Android kill the app in the background, then come back to it.
Steps: [{"fill": true}, {"fault": "kill_in_background"}, {"fault": "relaunch"}, {"settle": 6}]
Result: lost_state: 6 of 6 filled fields changed or emptied
Fields lost (before -> after): {'field_name': ['Ravi Kumar', ''], 'field_email': ['ravi@example.com', ''], 'field_phone': ['9876543210', ''], 'field_address': ['12 MG Road', ''], 'field_city': ['Bengaluru', ''], 'field_pincode': ['560001', '']}

## Diagnosis
Root cause: The checkout form's six fields are plain `mutableStateOf` properties on `CheckoutViewModel` (CheckoutViewModel.kt:14-19), and the ViewModel has no `SavedStateHandle` or any other persistence. CheckoutScreen binds each field directly to `vm.name`, `vm.email`, etc. (CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72). When Android kills the process in the background, the ViewModel and its in-memory state are destroyed. On relaunch, the route is restored via `rememberSaveable` (MainActivity.kt:62), so the user lands back on Checkout, but `viewModel()` creates a fresh `CheckoutViewModel` with every field blank. The route survives process death, but the form data does not.
Fix approach: Back the form state with `SavedStateHandle`: take `SavedStateHandle` in the ViewModel constructor and implement each field as `savedStateHandle.getStateFlow` or `savedStateHandle.mutableStateOf` (for example `var name by savedStateHandle.saveable { mutableStateOf("") }` from `androidx.compose.runtime.saveable`), so values are written to the saved-state bundle and restored after process death. The default `viewModel()` factory supplies a SavedStateHandle automatically, so the call site can stay unchanged. Alternatively, use `rememberSaveable` for each field in the composable, but the ViewModel approach keeps the state alongside the placeOrder logic.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:13-19 - ViewModel with no constructor arguments; six fields stored as plain mutableStateOf with no saved-state backing; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:1-10 - no SavedStateHandle import or usage anywhere in the ViewModel; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:34 - `vm: CheckoutViewModel = viewModel()` creates a fresh ViewModel with default state when the process is restored; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72 - each OutlinedTextField is bound directly to a ViewModel property, so the UI shows whatever the ViewModel holds, which is blank after restore; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:62 - the route is saved with rememberSaveable, so the user returns to the checkout screen but the form data is not restored; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:80 - CheckoutScreen is reached via the restored route, confirming the screen comes back while its state is lost

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt

## Regression test
Add a JVM unit test `CheckoutViewModelProcessDeathTest` in src/test. Create `CheckoutViewModel(SavedStateHandle())`, set name/email/phone/address/city/pincode to known values, then copy the handle's saved state into a new `SavedStateHandle` (simulating restore after process death) and construct a second `CheckoutViewModel` with it. Assert that all six fields in the second instance equal the originals and that `isComplete` is true. Before the fix, the no-arg ViewModel does not compile against a SavedStateHandle constructor, or the restored fields are empty, so the test fails. After the fix, it passes.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

package com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.foundation.rememberScrollState
import androidx.compose.foundation.text.KeyboardOptions
import androidx.compose.foundation.verticalScroll
import androidx.compose.material3.Button
import androidx.compose.material3.Card
import androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.testTag
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose.viewModel
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.OrderRepository
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.ProductRepository
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.priceLabel

@Composable
fun CheckoutScreen(
    productId: Int,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    vm: CheckoutViewModel = viewModel(),
) {
    val product = ProductRepository.cached(productId)
    val context = LocalContext.current
    val orders = remember { OrderRepository(context) }

    val placedId = vm.orderId
    if (placedId != null) {
        Column(modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(24.dp).testTag("order_confirmed"), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
            Text("Order placed 🎉", style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineSmall)
            Text("Order $placedId is on its way to ${vm.city}.", modifier = Modifier.testTag("order_id"))
        }
        return
    }

    Column(
        modifier = modifier
            .fillMaxSize()
            .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())
            .padding(16.dp)
            .testTag("checkout_screen"),
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
    ) {
        if (product != null) {
            Card(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
                Row(Modifier.padding(16.dp), horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween) {
                    Text("${product.emoji} ${product.name}", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f))
                    Text(product.priceLabel(), style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, modifier = Modifier.testTag("checkout_total"))
                }
            }
        }

        Text("Delivery details", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
        CheckoutField("Full name", vm.name, { vm.name = it }, "field_name")
        CheckoutField("Email", vm.email, { vm.email = it }, "field_email", KeyboardType.Email)
        CheckoutField("Phone", vm.phone, { vm.phone = it }, "field_phone", KeyboardType.Phone)

private fun CheckoutField(

) {

        onValueChange = onChange,
        label = { Text(label) },
        singleLine = true,
        keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = keyboard),
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().testTag(tag),
    )
}
